In addition, children must be properly restrained in an appropriate child restraint or seat belt based on age and size, and children under 13 are generally required to be properly restrained regardless of seating position. Always follow the specific age/size child restraint requirements in Oklahoma law.

question: True or false: A motorist turning left must yield to an oncoming bicyclist just like they would yield to an oncoming vehicle.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if the bicyclist is on the sidewalk.,d:Only if signs indicate to yield to bicycles
note: True. When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, including bicyclists, just as you would to oncoming motor vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver passes you in a no-passing zone, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from cutting in.,b:Pull off the road.,c:Slow down to let the other driver safely return to the lane.,d:Maintain your speed and lane position.
note: If another driver is passing you in a no-passing zone, you should not speed up or try to block them. Instead, maintain or slightly reduce your speed so the passing driver can safely return to your lane as soon as possible.

question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to them,b:Proceed as usual; they must yield,c:Flash your lights to make them aware
note: You must always yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane. Be prepared to stop and give them extra time to cross safely.

question: A single dashed yellow line between opposing lanes indicates:
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Passing is prohibited.,d:This lane is for bicycles only.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline means traffic in both directions may pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only if the bus is stopped in your lane,b:When the bus is stopped with red lights flashing and/or its stop arm extended,c:Only if children are visible crossing the road
note: On a standard two-lane highway (one lane in each direction), traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and/or its stop arm extended, unless a specific state law provides a clearly signed exception.

question: What does a steady yellow X above a reversible lane tell drivers?
options: a:The lane is about to close; you should clear it.,b:The lane will soon change to a green arrow.,c:Drivers may continue to drive normally in that lane.,d:The lane is reserved for buses only.
note: A steady yellow X above a reversible lane warns that the lane signal will soon change to a red X; you should prepare to leave that lane safely.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Wait at the scene until the police arrive regardless of circumstances.,b:Do nothing more and drive away.,c:Leave a written note with your name and contact information and briefly describe the accident.
note: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must stop, make a reasonable effort to find the owner, and if unsuccessful, leave a written note in a secure, visible place on the vehicle with your name, contact information, and a brief description of the accident. You must also report the collision to law enforcement if required by your state’s reporting thresholds.

question: Temporary signs used in construction and maintenance areas usually have what colors?
options: a:Yellow background with blue writing,b:Red background with green writing,c:Orange background with black writing
note: Temporary work zone and construction signs are typically orange with black letters or symbols.

question: Is it true that bridges and ramps can freeze before the main roadway?
options: a:Only at night.,b:TRUE,c:Only on mountain roads.,d:FALSE
note: Bridges and ramps are exposed to air on all sides and can become icy more quickly than the adjacent road surface; use extra caution.

question: When an authorized emergency vehicle using lights and/or sirens is approaching, you should:
options: a:Speed up to stay ahead of it.,b:Ignore and keep driving.,c:Pull to the right edge of the roadway and stop until it passes.
note: When an authorized emergency vehicle using lights and/or sirens is approaching, you must immediately pull as close as practicable to the right edge or curb of the roadway and stop, clear of any intersection, and remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed. If you are in an intersection when it approaches, clear the intersection before pulling to the right and stopping.

question: True or false: Large vehicles can have blind spots extending up to 200 feet behind them.
options: a:Only when towing trailers,b:True,c:Only for certain trucks,d:False
note: Large commercial vehicles can have very large blind spots behind them—often up to 200 feet or more. Avoid following too closely, as the driver may not see you if you are within this blind area.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which direction should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:Toward the side of the road (right).,c:Toward the center of the road (left).,d:Turn on hazard lights and leave wheels straight.
note: When parking on a hill without a curb—whether uphill or downhill—turn the front wheels toward the edge of the road (to the right). This way, if the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what is that hand signal indicating?
options: a:Speeding up.,b:Right turn.,c:Left turn.,d:Stopping.
note: A driver's left arm and hand extended upward indicate a right turn. A left arm straight out indicates a left turn, and a left arm extended downward indicates slowing or stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Any time you change lanes, pull into or out of a parking space, or enter traffic from a parking area or alley.,b:Only when making a U-turn.,c:Only when turning left at an intersection.,d:Never if no other vehicles are present.
note: You should signal for every intended lateral movement so other drivers are aware of your intentions, including any time you change lanes, pull into or out of a parking space, or enter traffic from a parking area or alley.

question: When being tailgated, what should you do to reduce collision risk?
options: a:Change lanes immediately without signaling.,b:Increase the space in front of your vehicle and avoid sudden braking.,c:Brake suddenly to teach the tailgater a lesson.,d:Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
note: If someone is tailgating, increase the space in front of your vehicle and avoid sudden braking or maneuvers. When safe, change lanes or otherwise allow the tailgater to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is unlawful at which locations?
options: a:On hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings.,b:Only on highways.,c:Only when two lanes are present.
note: Passing is unsafe and generally unlawful on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings, as well as in other clearly marked no-passing zones where you cannot safely see oncoming traffic.

question: Which of the following does NOT occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:You are less alert.,b:Your reflexes and reaction time speed up.,c:Your judgment of speed and distance becomes distorted.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, reduces alertness, and distorts judgment of speed and distance; it does not speed up reflexes or reaction time.

question: On average, how many standard alcoholic drinks does the body eliminate per hour?
options: a:One drink per hour.,b:None — alcohol accumulates indefinitely.,c:Two drinks per hour.,d:Three drinks per hour.
note: The average person's body metabolizes about one standard drink per hour, though many factors affect actual impairment and processing time.

question: What helps you avoid the need for emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Looking ahead and keeping a safe following distance,b:Honing your horn frequently,c:Staying in the right lane only
note: Maintaining a safe following distance and scanning ahead lets you react to problems without sudden stops.

question: When driving near large trucks, what should other drivers allow for?
options: a:That large trucks require a longer stopping distance.,b:That large trucks produce less noise and are easier to hear.,c:That trucks always have smaller blind spots than cars.,d:That trucks can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks need more room to stop and have large blind spots; smaller vehicles should stay where truck drivers can see them and avoid locations where the truck blocks their view of traffic.

question: What is the only thing that can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time,b:Eating fatty foods,c:Drinking coffee
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol and lower BAC; nothing else speeds this process.

question: Which of the following helps prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive in the shoulder if it starts to rain,b:Always use cruise control,c:Maintain good tire tread depth and proper inflation and reduce speed in rain
note: Good tread and proper tire pressure, plus reduced speed in wet conditions, reduce hydroplaning risk.

question: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, after a train passes you should:
options: a:Honk before crossing to alert any other trains.,b:Wait until you can see down all tracks and be sure no other trains are coming.,c:Proceed immediately as soon as the first train clears.,d:Cross while watching for oncoming cars.
note: After a train passes, you must wait until you can see clearly down all tracks and are sure no other trains are approaching before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather.,b:New drivers.,c:Human error (driver mistakes).
note: Most crashes occur because of human error — such as inattention, failing to see other vehicles, speeding, or other driver mistakes — rather than weather or vehicle issues.

question: Drowsy drivers may:
options: a:Drive poorly and appear intoxicated,b:Drive better than usual,c:Always be alert after drinking coffee
note: Drowsiness severely impairs driving ability. Drowsy drivers may weave, react slowly, and drive in a way that resembles intoxication. Coffee or other stimulants cannot be relied on to make a drowsy driver safe.

question: Under normal driving conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
options: a:Four seconds.,b:Two seconds.,c:Three seconds.,d:One second.
note: Under normal driving conditions, you should follow the vehicle ahead by at least three seconds. Use a fixed object to count: when the vehicle in front passes it, you should pass it no sooner than three seconds later. Increase this distance in poor weather, at higher speeds, or when following large vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the lane farthest from your original lane.,b:Into the lane closest to your original lane (usually the leftmost lane).,c:Into the rightmost lane on the one-way street.,d:Into any lane as long as you signal.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, you must turn into the lane closest to you that is going in your direction of travel, usually the leftmost lane on the one-way street, unless signs or lane markings indicate otherwise.

question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move.,b:Look only in the left side mirror.,c:Check the rearview mirror only.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check the blind spot that mirrors do not show.

question: What is the best way to avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options:
a: Call a taxi only if you feel very intoxicated.
b: Say 'No thanks' if you are offered alcohol and you plan to drive.
c: Decide before you begin drinking that you will not drive and arrange alternate transportation.
note: Deciding before you begin drinking that you will not drive and arranging alternate transportation is the best way to avoid alcohol‑related crashes. You should plan ahead for a sober driver, taxi, rideshare, or public transportation and never rely on how you “feel” after drinking.

question: When driving in snow or ice you should:
options:
a: Use cruise control to maintain steady speed.
b: Make speed and directional changes more gradually and avoid using cruise control.
c: Drive as you would in normal conditions.
note: On snow or ice, you should reduce speed, make speed and directional changes gradually, increase following distance, and avoid using cruise control because it can cause loss of traction.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use:
options:
a: High-beam headlights.
b: Parking lights only.
c: Low-beam headlights.
note: In rain or fog, use low‑beam headlights. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and reduce visibility, and parking lights alone are not sufficient or legal as a substitute for headlights while driving.

question: After stopping for a train at a crossing, what should you check for before proceeding?
options:
a: Only that the gates are up.
b: Look for a second train and ensure all warning signals have stopped.
c: That the first train cleared the nearest track regardless of other tracks.
d: Only that no cars are behind you.
note: After a train passes, do not proceed until you are sure all tracks are clear, all warning devices have stopped, and the gates are fully raised. Always look and listen for a second train on any adjacent tracks before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you enter an intersection if doing so will leave you blocking it when the light turns red?
options:
a: Yes — if you entered on a yellow light.
b: Yes — if you entered on a green light.
c: No — never enter unless you can clear the intersection completely.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it, even on a green or yellow light. Entering when you cannot clear the intersection can leave you blocking cross traffic and may result in a citation.

question: Why is driving at night more dangerous than during daylight?
options: a:The road surface is always more slippery at night.,b:Traffic laws are less enforced at night.,c:You cannot see as far ahead at night due to reduced visibility and headlight glare.,d:Your reaction time is always slower at night.
note: Reduced visibility and glare from headlights limit how far ahead you can see, making night driving more hazardous.

question: If you are emotionally upset from an incident at work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin driving home.,b:Turn the radio up loudly to distract yourself.,c:Drive fast to let off steam on the road.
note: Drivers who are upset should calm down before driving to avoid impaired judgment and dangerous actions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked cars to your right, where should you steer?
options: a:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,b:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,c:A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,d:Toward the parked cars to avoid traffic.
note: When faced with hazards on both sides, steer a middle course between oncoming vehicles and parked cars to maximize clearance.

question: Driving while distracted generally causes drivers to:
options: a:React faster to hazards,b:React more slowly to hazards,c:Never be involved in collisions
note: Distractions slow reaction times and increase the chance of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,c:You may turn after yielding to pedestrians.,d:Stop.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow. You may not proceed in the direction of the arrow while it is red.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company later and drive away.,b:Wait briefly,c:Only report it if there is visible damage.,d:Leave a note with your name
note: If you strike a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must leave a note in a secure, visible place on the vehicle with your name, contact information, and a brief description of the incident, and you must promptly report the collision to law enforcement if required by state law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should drivers do when approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Increase their speed to get through quickly.,b:Come to a complete stop every time.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Turn on hazard lights and proceed.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic as necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle in which of the following situations?
options: a:Only when the light is red,b:Only at stop signs,c:At a stop sign,d:At stop signs, red lights, and when directed by a police officer or traffic control person
note: You must stop at stop signs, at red traffic lights, and whenever directed to stop by a police officer or traffic control person. The question and options are incomplete because they suggest you are only required to stop at stop signs, which is not accurate.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what should you assume and do?
options: a:Speed up to pass quickly.,b:Slam on your brakes as you approach.,c:Assume the driver may open the door; use extra caution.
note: When passing a vehicle that is parked at the curb, assume someone may open a door or pull out. Slow down if needed, leave extra space, and be prepared to stop or move away from the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a reversible lane displays a red X, you should:
options: a:Drive only if no oncoming traffic is visible,b:Never drive in that lane,c:Use it to pass slowly
note: A red X over a reversible lane means that lane is closed to traffic in your direction. You must never drive in a lane showing a red X.

question: In a vehicle equipped with airbags, where is the safest place for children age 12 and under to ride?
options: a:The pickup bed.,b:The back seat.,c:Between the front seats.,d:The front seat.
note: Children age 12 and under are safest riding in the back seat, properly restrained in an appropriate child safety seat or seat belt. Front airbags can cause serious injury to children in a crash, so they should not ride in the front seat when a back seat is available.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part (lap and shoulder) seat belt system, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the lap belt since it is enough.,b:Use neither if you are driving slowly.,c:Use both the lap belt and the shoulder belt together.,d:Use only the shoulder belt and leave the lap belt unbuckled.
note: Wear both the lap and shoulder portions of a two-part seat belt system; using only one part reduces protection.

question: When changing lanes, which behavior should you avoid?
options: a:Checking over your shoulder to verify your blind spot.,b:Changing lanes abruptly without signaling.,c:Checking mirrors for other vehicles.,d:Using your turn signal ahead of time.
note: Never change lanes abruptly or without signaling; always check mirrors and blind spots before moving over.

question: What does a reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle signify?
options: a:It is a school bus.,b:It is an ambulance.,c:It is a slow-moving vehicle (25 mph or less).
note: A reflective orange triangle with a red border on the rear of a vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle emblem. It indicates the vehicle is designed to travel at speeds of 25 mph or less, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn vehicles.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Black,b:Yellow,c:Red,d:White
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:When there isn't room on the far side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks.,b:Only in towns with frequent train traffic.,c:Only when transporting two or more young children.
note: Never stop on the tracks; only cross if you can fully clear them. You must stop before the tracks if there is not enough room on the far side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks. Expect trains at any time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your original lane after passing, you should:
options: a:Flash your headlights to signal the other driver,b:Beep your horn once,c:Be able to see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror
note: Before returning to your original lane after passing, make sure you can clearly see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and that there is enough space to move back safely.

question: What happens as your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases?
options: a:You become more sober.,b:You become more coordinated and alert.,c:You become more intoxicated and impaired.,d:Your driving reflexes improve.
note: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, you become more intoxicated and impaired. Higher BAC levels reduce judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making driving increasingly unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: An approaching driver fails to dim high beams. Where should you look to avoid being blinded?
options: a:Directly into the approaching headlights.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,d:Toward the left side of the road.
note: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, avoid looking directly at the headlights. Instead, glance toward the right side of the road (the right edge line) to reduce glare while still keeping track of your lane position.

question: To safely cross a railroad track you should:
options: a:Look and listen both ways and proceed only when safe,b:Cross quickly if you see a train in the distance,c:Only look when the red lights are flashing
note: To safely cross a railroad track, always look and listen in both directions for approaching trains and proceed only when you are sure it is safe and all signals indicate you may cross.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous?
options: a:Distance and speed of other vehicles are harder to judge in the dark,b:Speed limits increase at night,c:There are more pedestrians at night
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to judge distances and speeds; you can only see as far as your headlights allow.

question: What should you do first when visibility is reduced?
options: a:Turn on your windshield wipers,b:Turn on your headlights,c:Reduce your speed
note: When visibility is reduced, you should first make sure you can be seen by others by turning on your headlights. You should also reduce your speed, but ensuring your lights are on is typically the first required action in low-visibility conditions.

question: When you see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal, what should you do?
options: a:Stop if it is safe to do so, because a red arrow is about to appear.,b:Proceed with the turn without yielding.,c:Merge into the lane pointed by the arrow immediately.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected turn is ending and a red arrow will follow; stop if you can do so safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roundabout, you should slow down and do what?
options: a:Yield to vehicles already circulating in the roundabout,b:Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing,c:Do both a and b
note: When entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield both to pedestrians and bicyclists in crosswalks and to vehicles already circulating in the roundabout.

question: Which of the following is a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Always using turn signals correctly.,b:Weaving between lanes and erratic driving behavior.,c:Consistently driving slower than traffic with no other signs.
note: Signs of impairment include weaving between lanes, erratic speed changes, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down and proceed cautiously.,b:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when safe.,c:Merge to the right and continue driving.,d:Only stop if another vehicle is present.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are in a collision,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation,c:Only if you are cited and arrested
note: You must carry proof of financial responsibility (insurance) and present it to a law enforcement officer upon request when you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where must you stop at a stop sign that has no marked crosswalk?
options: a:Only after entering the intersection,b:At least 20 feet before the sign,c:Before entering the intersection
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, you must make a complete stop before entering the intersection, at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you have a view of approaching traffic.

question: Which of these is a dangerous driving habit in work zones?
options: a:Using your headlights,b:Obeying posted speed limits,c:Following another vehicle too closely
note: Following another vehicle too closely (tailgating) is especially dangerous in work zones because traffic may slow or stop suddenly and workers or equipment may be present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?
options: a:Follow what other cars are doing regardless of the guard's instructions.,b:Assume the guard is not authorized and proceed normally.,c:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
note: When a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must obey their instructions and use extra caution, regardless of what other drivers are doing.

question: What is the only reliable way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol,b:Drink coffee to sober up,c:Exercise to speed alcohol elimination
note: Only time allows the body to eliminate alcohol and reduce BAC; other methods such as coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not speed up alcohol metabolism.

question: What color pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Blue.,b:Yellow.,c:White.,d:Red.
note: Yellow pavement markings divide lanes carrying traffic in opposite directions. White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision,b:To express frustration with slow drivers,c:To encourage another driver to speed up
note: Use your horn only when it may help prevent a collision or warn others of a hazard. Do not use it to express anger, frustration, or to pressure other drivers.

question: If poor weather reduces visibility, what should you do regarding following distance?
options: a:Follow at the same distance as during clear weather.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Speed up to clear the hazard more quickly.,d:Increase your following distance to allow more time to react.
note: When visibility is reduced by weather such as rain, fog, or snow, you should increase your following distance to give yourself more time to see hazards and stop safely.

question: To drive safely at night you should:
options: a:Reduce following distance to keep traffic flowing,b:Increase following distance,c:Use high beams at all times
note: At night, you should increase your following distance so you have more time to react within the limited range of your headlights. Also ensure your lights are working properly and avoid driving when drowsy.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane.,d:Turn without signaling if no cars are nearby.
note: Yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians crossing in the path of your turn before turning left.

question: Why should you avoid following other vehicles too closely?
options: a:You may not see the road between the cars,b:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals,c:You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly
note: Following too closely reduces your time to react and increases the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: For quick, controlled turns, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?
options: a:One on the top and one on the bottom of the wheel.,b:Next to each other on top of the wheel.,c:On opposite sides of the wheel (such as the 9 and 3 o’clock positions).
note: Placing your hands on opposite sides of the wheel (such as the 9 and 3 o’clock positions) gives better control for quick, controlled turns and steering adjustments.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is correct?
options: a:All prescription and over-the-counter medications are always safe.,b:Only illegal drugs impair driving.,c:Even over-the-counter medications can impair your driving.,d:If you do not feel drowsy after a prescription, it cannot affect your driving.
note: Even over-the-counter and some prescription medications can impair your driving. It is illegal to drive under the influence of any drug that affects your ability to drive safely.

question: When driving in an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Always stop at the curb before crossing.,b:Only cross at marked crosswalks.,c:Wait for you to wave them across.,d:Run out into the street without looking.
note: Children may fail to recognize danger and could run into the street unexpectedly; when driving where children are playing, slow down and be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you proceed at an intersection controlled by a stop sign but with no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before entering the intersection, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Stop at least 20 feet before the intersection regardless of layout.
note: Stop before entering the intersection and yield to cross traffic and pedestrians; proceed only when safe.

question: If you have a tire blowout while driving, what actions should you take?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas, do not brake immediately, and gradually slow down to a safe spot off the road.,b:Brake hard immediately to stop as soon as possible.,c:Keep accelerating to maintain stability.,d:Turn sharply and continue driving at normal speed.
note: On a blowout, lift off the accelerator, avoid sudden braking, steer smoothly, slow gradually, and pull off the road when safe.

question: If a police officer stops you, how should you behave while waiting?
options: a:Get your documents from the glovebox before the officer reaches your car,b:Stay in your vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer,c:Unbuckle your seat belt and open the window partly
note: Remain in the vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel; wait until the officer requests documents or further action.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow traffic signal mean?
options: a:The signal is never used.,b:Drivers may turn in the arrow direction without caution.,c:Same meaning as a circular yellow light; prepare to stop.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected-turn indication is ending; it has the same meaning as a circular yellow light for that movement—slow and prepare to stop, clearing the intersection if you are already in it.

question: How should you check your blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:By turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,b:By using your turn signal then changing lanes.,c:Only by looking in your side mirrors.,d:By checking the rearview mirror only.
note: Blind spots cannot be seen with mirrors alone. Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and then turn your head and quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to check your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Partially enter to establish your right-of-way,b:Do not enter the intersection until you can get completely through it,c:Enter and wait for traffic to clear
note: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it fully to avoid blocking it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it acceptable to stop in a travel lane to look up an address or drop off passengers?
options: a:Only in emergencies.,b:No — you should not stop in a travel lane.,c:Yes,d:Only during daylight hours.
note: No. You should not stop in a travel lane for non-emergency reasons. If you need to look up an address or drop off passengers, continue until you can safely pull off the road and stop out of the flow of traffic.

question: After a minor collision that is blocking traffic, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the road.,b:Remain where your vehicle is until police arrive.,c:Leave the scene immediately if no one is hurt.,d:Push your vehicle into the nearest lane to speed traffic.
note: If possible after a minor crash, move vehicles off the traveled portion of the road to keep traffic flowing; do not leave the scene without exchanging information.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you always drive more slowly than the surrounding traffic?
options: a:No — driving too slowly can block traffic and be dangerous.,b:Yes — it helps with defensive driving.,c:Only in residential areas.,d:Yes — slower driving is always safer.
note: No. You should not always drive more slowly than surrounding traffic. Driving significantly slower than the normal flow can block traffic and create a hazard, and in some situations it is illegal. Adjust your speed to the posted limit and road, traffic, and weather conditions.

question: To help others see you as daylight fades, you should use:
options: a:High-beam headlights at all times.,b:Emergency flashers only.,c:Parking lights.,d:Low-beam headlights.
note: As daylight fades, turn on your low-beam headlights so that you can see and be seen. Do not rely on parking lights alone while driving, and reserve high beams for open roads without oncoming traffic or vehicles ahead of you.

question: What should you do if a tire blows out while driving?
options: a:Keep driving at the same speed until you reach a service area.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly,c:Slam on the brakes immediately.
note: Do not brake hard; maintain control, gradually reduce speed, and steer to a safe place to stop.

question: If another vehicle appears likely to collide with you, what should you do to warn them?
options: a:Turn on your emergency lights only.,b:Wave your arms out the window.,c:Sound your horn to alert the other driver.
note: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians in imminent-danger situations so they can react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle when:
options: a:Only if the opposite-side line is broken,b:The vehicle ahead moves to the right to let you pass,c:The yellow line on your side is broken and it is safe to pass
note: You may pass across double yellow lines only when the yellow line next to your lane is broken and passing is safe.

question: True or false: It is legal for a car to share a single lane with a motorcycle.
options: a:Only at low speeds,b:If both drivers agree,c:False,d:True
note: False. Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane; it is unlawful and unsafe in most states for a car to share a single lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle.

question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally in the street (not in a crosswalk), what must you do?
options: a:Drive on; they are at fault,b:Honk to make them move faster,c:Yield and stop for them
note: You must yield to pedestrians regardless of whether they are in a crosswalk; stop if necessary to avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should a driver who is traveling much slower than the posted speed do when traffic is backing up behind them?
options: a:Always maintain their speed and position,b:Refuse to allow others to pass,c:Pull off the roadway to allow others to pass
note: If you are driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic and causing a backup, you should, when safe, pull off the roadway or move to the right to allow other vehicles to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, what sequence of actions should you take?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights and merge.,b:Check only your rearview mirror then change lanes.,c:Signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, and then change lanes when safe.,d:Signal and immediately move over.
note: When changing lanes on a highway, you should: signal your intention, check your mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Change lanes only when it is safe to do so.

question: A flashing yellow arrow at an intersection means drivers may:
options: a:Merge into the lane without yielding.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow means you may make the indicated turn, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Is it ever safe to stop on railroad tracks if moving with traffic across them?
options: a:False — you should not stop on railroad tracks.,b:True — brief stops are acceptable.,c:True — only if traffic is moving slowly.
note: You must never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Only proceed to cross if there is enough space on the far side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multi-lane highway, what must you ensure?
options: a:The passing lane is clear before you move into it.,b:You only pass on the right regardless of lane markings.,c:You never signal when changing lanes.,d:You drive at the exact same speed as the vehicle being passed.
note: Before passing on a multi-lane highway, make sure the lane you intend to use is clear, signal your lane change, pass safely without exceeding the speed limit, and then return to your lane when it is safe.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal indicates that which light will appear next?
options: a:Steady red,b:Flashing yellow,c:Steady green
note: A steady yellow light warns that a steady red light will soon follow. You should slow down and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn off the ignition immediately.,b:Ease off the gas and steer in the direction of the skid.,c:Pump the brakes rapidly and steer opposite the skid.,d:Brake as hard as possible and hold the wheel tightly.
note: If your vehicle starts to skid, the first thing you should do is ease off the accelerator (and avoid hard braking), then steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go (generally the direction of the skid). This helps you regain control. Do not brake hard, turn off the ignition, or steer sharply in the opposite direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a designated left-turn lane with oncoming traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the left of the center lane immediately,b:Turn your front wheels left to be ready to go,c:Signal about 100 feet before the turn and keep wheels straight until safe to turn
note: When preparing for a left turn, signal about 100 feet before the turn (or more if required by local law), enter the designated left-turn lane, and keep your wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This prevents your vehicle from being pushed into oncoming traffic if you are struck from behind.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do at a yield sign when entering another roadway?
options: a:Speed up to merge quickly.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic already in the roadway or approaching closely.,c:Always come to a full stop even if the road is clear.,d:Yield only to traffic on your left.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Yield the right-of-way to traffic already on the roadway and to any closely approaching traffic or pedestrians before you enter or cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or false: You may exceed the posted speed limit to pass another vehicle.
options: a:Only on highways,b:False,c:Only when safe,d:True
note: You must obey the posted speed limit at all times. You may not exceed the speed limit in order to pass another vehicle, even if you believe it would be safer or quicker.

question: Motorcycles on the roadway are entitled to:
options: a:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles,b:Use of bicycle lanes only,c:Half of a lane's width
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full lane width, just like other vehicles. Other drivers should not share a lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you tell it's safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:After traveling at least 500 feet past the vehicle.,b:When you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.,c:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,d:Only after the other driver signals you to re-enter.
note: You should not return to your driving lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, indicating you have enough space to move back safely without cutting the other driver off.

question: Which statement is true about backing your vehicle?
options: a:Backing is only dangerous for large vehicles and safe for small ones.,b:Backing is safe if you have a helper,c:Backing is always potentially dangerous because visibility is limited.,d:Backing is never dangerous at low speed.
note: Backing is always potentially dangerous because rear visibility is limited. Use extra caution, check mirrors and blind spots, and use a helper if available.

question: What is 'highway hypnosis' and how can it occur?
options: a:A state of reduced alertness from staring ahead for long periods.,b:A condition that can be reduced by frequent rest stops.,c:A result of too much sleep before driving.
note: Highway hypnosis is a state of reduced alertness or drowsy, trance‑like driving that can occur when you stare straight ahead at the road for long periods without actively scanning or taking breaks. It increases crash risk and is prevented by staying alert, taking regular breaks, and varying your focus.

question: Which statement describes a work zone?
options: a:Does not require drivers to slow down.,b:Is marked with black and white signs only.,c:May be stationary or moving and requires extra caution.
note: A work zone is an area where road construction, maintenance, or utility work is occurring. It may be stationary or moving (such as a moving striping or sweeping operation) and is typically marked with orange signs, cones, or other devices. Drivers must use extra caution and usually slow down, and in many states face increased fines for violations in work zones.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do regarding vehicle lights?
options: a:Use only parking lights.,b:Keep lights off.,c:Turn on headlights (low beams)
note: Turn on headlights at dusk or on overcast days and use low beams when near other vehicles to reduce glare.

question: A driver's license is legally considered which of the following?
options: a:A right,b:A requirement.,c:A privilege
note: A driver license is a privilege granted under state law, not an inherent right.

question: If someone is tailgating you on a two-lane road and you cannot change lanes, what is the best action?
options: a:Speed up to increase the distance.,b:Reduce speed slowly to encourage them to pass.,c:Brake sharply to warn them.,d:Pull off the road immediately and stop.
note: Slow down gradually (without sudden braking) to increase the space in front of you and encourage the tailgater to pass when it is safe. If possible and safe, change lanes or pull over briefly to let them by.

question: When road surfaces are slippery due to rain or ice, what should you do?
options: a:Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.,b:Maintain the posted speed limit no matter what.,c:Drive faster to get through the area quickly.,d:Slow down and drive more cautiously than usual.
note: Reduce speed at the first sign of slippery conditions to maintain control, increase following distance, and allow for longer stopping distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat an intersection controlled by a flashing red light?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping.,b:Come to a full stop,c:Stop and remain stopped as long as the light is flashing.,d:Only stop if other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a full stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe. You do not have to remain stopped the entire time the light is flashing.

question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean?
options: a:Passing allowed only at hill crests.,b:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,c:Passing is allowed for both directions.
note: Two solid yellow centerlines indicate traffic moving in opposite directions and prohibit passing from either side.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:When it is safe to change lanes.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:Only to pass large vehicles.,d:Any time regardless of conditions.
note: Dashed white lines separate traffic lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross them to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking traffic and signaling.

question: When parking facing uphill on a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Toward the curb.,b:Away from the curb.,c:Keep them straight ahead.,d:Turn them toward the middle of the road.
note: When parking facing uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will contact the curb and stop the vehicle from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What practice commonly blocks the smooth flow of traffic near an incident?
options: a:Using public transportation instead of a car.,b:Slowing down to look at a collision scene (rubbernecking).,c:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
note: Rubbernecking — slowing to look at a collision or incident scene — disrupts traffic flow, creates congestion, and can cause secondary collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with opposing traffic, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:As soon as you are one car length ahead.,b:When you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:Immediately after overtaking the front bumper.,d:Only after signaling twice.
note: On a two-lane road with opposing traffic, after passing, return to your lane only when you can clearly see the front of the passed vehicle (typically its headlights) in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe following distance before moving back.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a road where traffic is moving at 50–55 mph, when are you least likely to have an accident?
options: a:When you stay within that speed range and flow of traffic.,b:When you drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.,c:When you drive a few miles per hour slower than most vehicles.
note: Traveling smoothly with the flow of traffic (within posted limits) reduces differences in speed and reduces multi-vehicle crash risk.

question: If another driver cuts you off, what is the safest response?
options: a:Pull alongside and yell at the driver.,b:Flash your high beams rapidly at them.,c:Let it go and continue driving safely.,d:Speed up to retaliate.
note: To avoid road rage and risky behavior, don't take it personally — let it go and continue driving safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, the speed limit on a four-lane divided highway is:
options: a:45 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:70 mph.,d:35 mph.
note: On many four-lane divided highways in the U.S., the typical statutory (default) speed limit is 65–70 mph where not otherwise posted, and 70 mph is a common standard maximum in rural areas. Always obey the posted speed limit signs, which override any general default rule.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway safely you should:
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at about the same speed traffic is moving,b:Signal and expect freeway traffic to yield to you,c:Drive slowly to carefully check traffic
note: When merging, signal, yield to vehicles on the freeway, and match the speed of traffic to merge safely.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is correct?
options: a:Railroad crossings always have flashing lights and gates.,b:You may go around lowered gates if no train is visible.,c:You never need to stop unless a train is approaching.,d:It is against the law to drive around lowered crossing gates.
note: Driving around lowered railroad gates is illegal and dangerous; not all crossings have active warning devices, so obey signs and signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Drivers who arrived before you.,b:No one — you always go first.,c:Drivers on your left regardless of arrival order.,d:Only vehicles with flashing lights.
note: At a four-way stop, proceed in the order that vehicles arrive; yield to those who arrived before you. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on most country roads?
options: a:55 mph,b:35 mph,c:25 mph
note: On many rural two-lane undivided highways in the U.S., the statutory speed limit is 55 mph unless a different speed is posted. However, this can vary by state and by road type (for example, some states use 45 mph or 65 mph on certain rural roads). Always obey the posted speed limit and adjust your speed for conditions.

question: As you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution after checking for hazards.,b:Stop before crossing every time.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down, yield as necessary, check for cross traffic and other hazards, and proceed through the intersection with caution when it is safe.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing emergency lights, you must:
options: a:Slow down but stay in your lane,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle passes,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you
note: When you hear a siren or see flashing emergency lights approaching from any direction (unless you are in an intersection), you must immediately pull over to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop as soon as it is safe.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:There is a pedestrian crossing ahead.,b:A railroad crossing is ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,d:The road is one-way.
note: Double solid yellow lines in the center of a two-way road mean that passing is not permitted from either direction. You may cross them only when making a permitted left turn, entering or exiting a driveway or side road, or where specific legal exceptions apply.

question: True or false: Driving is a right guaranteed to all citizens.
options: a:False,b:Only for those over 18,c:Only for state residents,d:True
note: Driving is not a constitutional right; it is a privilege granted and regulated by each state. A driver’s license can be suspended or revoked for violations or unsafe driving, so driving is not guaranteed to all citizens.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in a school zone?
options: a:45 mph,b:25 mph,c:35 mph
note: In many states, the default speed limit in a school zone when children are present is 25 mph unless a different limit is specifically posted. However, school zone speed limits vary by state (often 15–25 mph) and are always controlled by posted signs, so drivers must obey the posted school zone speed limit for their jurisdiction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before changing lanes or attempting to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, and signal your intention.,b:Only signal, then change lanes without checking blind spots.,c:Rely solely on the rearview mirror to confirm it's safe.,d:Flash your headlights before moving over.
note: Always signal before changing lanes, check your mirrors, and turn your head to check blind spots to ensure it is safe before moving into another lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into your lane?
options: a:After signaling for at least two seconds.,b:When you feel you have enough speed,c:When the entire passed vehicle is visible in your rearview mirror.,d:When the passing maneuver is almost complete regardless of mirror view.
note: After passing, do not return to your original lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space to move back safely without cutting off the other driver.

question: When parking facing uphill on a road without a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels sharply to the left so the car will roll into traffic if it moves.,b:Keep the wheels straight ahead and leave the car in gear.,c:Turn the wheels away from the edge of the road.,d:Turn the wheels toward the edge of the road (to the right).
note: When parking facing uphill on a road without a curb, turn the front wheels toward the edge of the road (to the right). If the vehicle rolls, it will move away from the roadway instead of into traffic.

question: What does a flashing yellow X above a reversible lane mean?
options: a:The lane is about to change to a green arrow for through traffic.,b:The lane is about to be closed with a red X.,c:You may use the lane only to make a left turn.
note: A flashing yellow X over a reversible lane means the lane is for left turns only; you may use that lane only to make a left turn and not for through travel.

question: What is a good way to relieve fatigue on a long trip?
options: a:Drive with one eye closed for variety.,b:Do arm exercises every hour while driving.,c:Stop for a rest every two hours.,d:Keep driving without long breaks to maintain momentum.
note: To avoid fatigue on long trips, stop about every two hours for a short rest. If you feel drowsy, pull over in a safe place to rest or stop for the night.

question: What speed should you maintain while driving?
options: a:The speed of the vehicles around you regardless of conditions.,b:A speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.,c:Always the maximum speed allowed on that road.,d:The posted speed limit only.
note: You should always drive at a speed that is safe and appropriate for current road, traffic, and weather conditions, and never exceed the posted speed limit—even if other drivers are going faster.

question: What mindset should you have when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Expect workers to yield to motorists.,b:Slightly increase your speed to get through quickly.,c:Expect the unexpected and use extra caution.
note: In construction zones, expect the unexpected: workers, equipment, lane shifts, and sudden stops. Slow down, stay alert, and use extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following should you never do when turning left?
options: a:Signal your turn in advance.,b:Cut the corner and interfere with other traffic.,c:Slow down to a safe turning speed.,d:Yield to oncoming traffic when required.
note: You should never cut the corner when turning left, because this can put you into the path of oncoming or crossing traffic and cause a collision. Instead, stay in your lane and turn from the proper position.

question: Which type of pavement marking allows you to pass another vehicle when it is safe?
options: a:Double solid white lines.,b:A solid yellow line next to your lane.,c:A broken white line.,d:Double solid yellow lines.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with stop signs on all corners, who should you yield to after stopping?
options: a:Vehicles across from you regardless of arrival time.,b:No one; proceed immediately after stopping.,c:The driver who arrived before you.,d:Only vehicles on your left.
note: At a four-way stop, after coming to a complete stop, drivers proceed in the order in which they arrived. You must yield to any vehicle that reached the intersection before you. If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: What do orange background traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:General warning signs.,c:Construction and maintenance warning signs.
note: Orange background signs are used for temporary traffic control, especially construction, maintenance, and work-zone warnings.

question: What does a posted “No standing” sign generally mean?
options: a:You may never stop at that location for any reason.,b:You may park there if the driver remains with the vehicle.,c:You may park for up to 15 minutes.,d:You may stop temporarily only to pick up or drop off passengers.
note: A “No Standing” sign generally means you may stop temporarily only to pick up or drop off passengers. You may not park, wait, or load/unload merchandise there.

question: What do orange-colored highway signs typically indicate?
options: a:Regulatory instructions,b:A school zone ahead,c:Work or construction zones ahead
note: Orange-colored highway signs typically indicate work, construction, or maintenance zones and related warnings.

question: When should you avoid using your horn?
options: a:When visibility ahead is limited.,b:If you might hit another vehicle soon.,c:Near blind pedestrians and in situations where it may startle them.
note: Do not honk near blind pedestrians; use caution and yield so you don't endanger or startle them. Use your horn only when necessary to avoid a collision, such as when visibility is limited or you might hit another vehicle.

question: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers stopped behind the bus must remain stopped until:
options: a:All students have exited and are off the road.,b:The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.,c:Only until the bus driver signals with a hand gesture.,d:Children begin to cross the street.
note: When a school bus has flashing red lights and the stop arm extended, motorists must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing, the stop arm is retracted, and the bus starts moving again, unless a specific state law provides a clearly separated roadway exception.

question: In foggy conditions you should:
options: a:Turn on your low-beam headlights,b:Turn on your hazard lights only,c:Drive at the posted maximum speed
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog; high beams can reflect off the fog and reduce visibility. Turn on your headlights (not just parking lights) whenever visibility is significantly reduced, and reduce your speed to match conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop completely even if clear.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,d:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic as necessary. You do not need to stop and you do not wait for a green light.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the safest action?
options: a:Stay in your vehicle and wait for help.,b:Get out and walk for help immediately.,c:Lie down in the car and go to sleep.
note: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, the safest action is usually to stay in your vehicle, which provides shelter and makes it easier for rescuers to find you. Run the engine only periodically for heat, ensure the exhaust pipe is clear of snow, and only leave the vehicle if you can clearly see safe help nearby.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,b:Brake hard to discourage the pass.,c:Maintain a steady speed and allow them to pass safely.
note: When being passed, do not speed up or interfere; maintain your speed (or slow slightly if needed) and let the other vehicle pass and re-enter safely.

question: If you hear a siren from an emergency vehicle behind you while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Safely pull over to the right edge of the road and stop.,b:Stop where you are immediately without signaling.,c:Speed up to get away from the emergency vehicle.,d:Ignore it and continue at the same speed.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches from behind with lights or siren, you must yield the right-of-way by safely pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping until it has passed, unless otherwise directed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what is required of the driver?
options: a:Accelerate and merge quickly.,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,c:Yield to traffic that is close enough to be a hazard.,d:Always come to a complete stop.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary. You must yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians that are close enough to be a hazard. A complete stop is only required if needed to avoid interfering with other road users.

question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind on an uphill grade, what should you remember?
options: a:The truck will speed up on hills to maintain traffic flow.,b:The truck may be traveling more slowly than the posted speed and passing may be unsafe.,c:You can always safely pass on the shoulder.,d:The truck will always be at the posted speed limit.
note: Large trucks often travel below the posted speed limit on uphill grades due to their weight and reduced climbing ability. On hills with limited visibility, passing may be unsafe and is often prohibited by signs or road markings.

question: Should you always check behind your vehicle for small children or bikes before backing up?
options: a:False — mirrors are sufficient.,b:True — always check behind your car before getting in and backing up.,c:False — it's unnecessary unless you hear something.
note: Before backing up, always walk around and check behind your vehicle for children, bicycles, toys, or other obstacles. Mirrors and cameras may not show objects very close to the rear of the vehicle.

question: How should you scan the roadway to prepare for hazards ahead?
options: a:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Continuously scan the entire road and roadsides rather than staring straight ahead.
note: Continuously scanning the roadway and sides helps you identify problems early and react safely.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should:
options: a:Drive more slowly directly behind the motorcycle,b:Be ready to use your horn frequently,c:Allow a larger following distance (about three to four seconds)
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly and are more vulnerable; allow extra following distance of at least three to four seconds.

question: Many crashes are caused by which of these driver behaviors?
options: a:Consistently yielding the right-of-way to others.,b:Regular mirror checks and blind spot checks.,c:Traveling too fast for the conditions.
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a common cause of crashes; always adjust speed to weather, traffic, and road conditions.

question: If you see pedestrians near the roadway where you are driving, how should you respond?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,b:Change lanes immediately without slowing.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.,d:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: Watch for pedestrians who may step into your path. Slow down, pass with caution, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer vs. wine) change how much it impairs you?
options: a:Mixed drinks are the only highly impairing beverages.,b:Beer impairs less than wine.,c:All alcoholic beverages can impair you equally depending on your BAC.,d:Wine impairs less than beer.
note: Impairment depends on the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream (BAC), not the type of drink. A standard serving of beer, wine, or distilled spirits contains roughly the same amount of alcohol and can impair you equally if they result in the same BAC.

question: If rain begins while you are driving and visibility is reduced, what should you do?
options: a:Drive at the maximum posted speed limit regardless of visibility.,b:Slow down and increase your following distance, using your headlights as needed.,c:Drive faster than surrounding traffic to get through the rain.
note: If rain begins and visibility is reduced, you should slow down, increase your following distance, and turn on your low‑beam headlights. If visibility becomes so poor that you cannot see the road or other vehicles at a safe distance, pull off the roadway to a safe location and wait for conditions to improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm is extended downward outside the vehicle, what does that hand signal mean?
options: a:The driver intends to turn right.,b:The driver intends to stop or slow.,c:The driver intends to turn left.
note: Left arm extended downward outside the vehicle indicates that the driver intends to slow down or stop. This is a standard hand signal used when brake lights are not visible or functioning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Rely only on the outside mirrors.,b:Look only at the inside rearview mirror.,c:Turn your head and look over the left or right shoulder to view the blind spot.,d:Use your horn to warn other drivers first.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then turn your head to look over the appropriate shoulder to check the blind spot. Mirrors alone do not show all areas around your vehicle.

question: Your blind spot refers to the area:
options: a:You cannot see without turning your head.,b:Directly behind your vehicle.,c:Visible in your rearview mirror.,d:Only next to your door.
note: Your blind spot is the area around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors. You must briefly turn your head and look to check these areas before changing lanes or merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?
options: a:No one — they have the right to turn.,b:Oncoming vehicles going straight.,c:Only vehicles that are overtaking them.
note: Drivers turning left must yield the right‑of‑way to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right, unless they have a protected left‑turn signal or are otherwise directed by traffic control devices.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing another vehicle prohibited?
options: a:On a hill or near the crest,b:In a legal passing zone when safe to do so,c:On a straightaway with clear vision,d:Only when a police officer directs you not to pass.
note: Do not pass on a curve or on a hill where you cannot see oncoming traffic; pass only where it is clearly safe and legal.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Slow down to reduce risk of falling asleep.,b:Turn up the car radio to keep alert.,c:Stop at regular intervals to rest and stretch.
note: Schedule regular stops to rest and stretch; short breaks prevent drowsiness better than other measures.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are you required to signal every time you pull away from a curb?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must use your turn signal anytime you pull away from a curb to indicate your intent.

question: If a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, what does that mean?
options: a:Drivers next to the broken line may pass when safe.,b:No passing by either direction at any time.,c:Drivers on both sides may pass.,d:Drivers next to the solid line may pass.
note: If a solid yellow line is next to a broken yellow line, drivers next to the broken line may pass when it is safe, while drivers next to the solid line must not pass.

question: When parallel parking downhill, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Sharply toward the curb or side of the road.,b:Away from the curb.,c:Keep them straight ahead.,d:Turn them toward the centerline.
note: When parking downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is being lowered or raised?
options: a:If you first look carefully both directions.,b:Only if you can do so without damaging the gate.,c:If a train is not too close.,d:Never drive around or under a moving or lowered gate.
note: Flashing lights, lowered gates, and bells mean you must stop and not cross the tracks until signals stop and gates are fully raised. Never go under or around a moving or lowered gate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How are fines typically changed for moving violations in construction/maintenance zones when workers are present?
options: a:Fines are reduced.,b:Fines are unchanged.,c:Fines are doubled.
note: In many states, including Oklahoma, fines for moving traffic violations in construction or maintenance work zones are increased—often doubled—when workers are present and proper advance warning signs are posted. Always reduce speed and drive with extra caution in work zones.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed from either direction at any time.,b:No passing is permitted at all.,c:Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line only.,d:Passing is allowed from the lane beside the solid line.
note: When a broken yellow line is alongside a solid yellow line, vehicles on the side with the broken line may pass when it is safe to do so. Vehicles on the side with the solid line may not pass.

question: How does increasing your vehicle’s speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:Doesn't change it.,b:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.,c:Decreases it.,d:Increases it.
note: As your speed increases, your peripheral field of vision narrows and you see less of what is happening to the sides. Higher speeds reduce your effective field of vision, so you must be especially alert for hazards.

question: What is a distraction while driving?
options: a:Anything that causes you to brake smoothly,b:Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving,c:Anything that takes your attention away from driving
note: A distraction is any activity that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from the driving task and can increase the risk of a collision.

question: Which of the following influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:Only the type of alcohol consumed.,b:Only the amount of food eaten.,c:The amount of food in the stomach.,d:None — everyone is affected the same way.
note: BAC is affected by how much you drink, how quickly you drink, your body weight, and whether you have eaten. Food in the stomach slows alcohol absorption but does not prevent impairment. Among the options given, only choice (c) correctly reflects a real factor that influences alcohol’s effects.

question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with sirens or flashing lights, what must you do immediately?
options: a:Pull to the right and turn on your hazard lights only.,b:Pull to the right side of the road and stop.,c:Pull to the right and slow down but keep moving.
note: You must immediately move to the right side of the road and stop (when safe to do so) to allow emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights to pass safely.

question: If a train is close enough or fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Cross at your own risk if no signals are active.,b:Do not cross the tracks until the train has fully passed.,c:Slow down and cross before the train arrives.
note: If a train is close enough or moving fast enough to be a danger, you must not cross the tracks. Wait until the train has completely passed and it is clearly safe before crossing, even if warning signals are not active.

question: Exiting the freeway onto a ramp that curves downhill, you should:
options: a:Begin braking only after you enter the curve.,b:Stop at the start of the ramp and then proceed slowly.,c:Maintain freeway speed until the end of the ramp.,d:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.
note: You should slow to a safe speed before entering a downhill, curved exit ramp. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skids or loss of control, especially on a downgrade.

question: What does a diamond-shaped road sign indicate?
options: a:Yield.,b:Stop.,c:Warning of a condition or hazard ahead.,d:Directional guidance.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert drivers to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings, and are usually yellow or orange.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Because you are moving faster than the bicycle.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.,d:Bicycles are required to ride on sidewalks.
note: Be cautious because oncoming traffic might not see you as you move out to pass a bicyclist; give cyclists plenty of space and only pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: Is every motor vehicle in Oklahoma required to have liability insurance?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Oklahoma law requires that every motor vehicle operated on public roads be covered by liability insurance (or an approved equivalent form of financial responsibility). Vehicles that are not operated on public roads may be exempt, but any vehicle being driven must be insured.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and you must stop on snow or ice, what is the correct braking technique?
options: a:Stay off the brakes and let the vehicle drift to a stop.,b:Pump the brakes manually,c:Release the brake and stomp it repeatedly.,d:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly so the ABS can operate.
note: If your vehicle has ABS, press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer normally. Do not pump the brakes; the ABS system automatically pumps them for you to help maintain steering control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is an important step to take before making a turn?
options: a:Close your eyes briefly to focus.,b:Always move into the left lane before turning.,c:Increase your speed to complete the turn quickly.,d:Check traffic in all directions including rear and sides.
note: Before making a turn, check traffic in all directions, including your rear and sides, and use your mirrors and signals to ensure it is safe to turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Never — always insist on your right-of-way.,b:Only when another driver signals you to do so.,c:Whenever yielding helps prevent a collision.,d:Only at uncontrolled intersections.
note: You should yield your legal right-of-way whenever doing so will help prevent a collision. Never insist on your right-of-way if it would create or worsen a dangerous situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the purpose of an advisory speed sign attached to a curve warning sign?
options: a:To indicate the only legal speed you may drive in any condition.,b:To show a recommended safe speed for that curve under ideal conditions.,c:To be ignored during rain,d:To mark the distance to the next town.
note: Advisory speed signs show a recommended safe speed for the curve under ideal conditions; drivers should slow further in bad weather or poor conditions.

question: When passing an emergency vehicle stopped on the right shoulder, drivers should:
options: a:Increase speed to pass quickly,b:Stop and offer assistance without checking conditions,c:Vacate the lane closest to the emergency vehicle or slow down
